summary: Chun-fang Yu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1966-1973) and under traditional teachers Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972-2001) and Columbia University (~2001-2019).

Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona, supervised by Robert M. Gimello and taught by Todd Brown, and also studied under traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Gangshar and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and at Oxford and St Antony's College (~1963-1967). He founded Naropa University in 1973.
Chönyi Drolma works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under teacher Ngawang Zangpo and traditional teachers Thinley Norbu Rinpoche and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.
Clare Carlisle is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1995-2002) and served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006-2011).

Claude Jacques was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under George Cœdès. He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Claudia Weber is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and under project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Cambridge (Queens' College, ~1791-1795), and served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College in 1801.

Claus Oetke was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974-1980), where he was a wissenschaftlicher Assistent (~1980-1985), before holding a post at Stockholm University (~1992-2012).
Claus Vogel was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1964-1967), the University of Marburg (~1967-1976), and the University of Bonn (1976).

Colette Caillat was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She served as Director at the University of Paris (~1966-1989) and was a member of the Institut de France and Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1987-2007).

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.

Collett Cox is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Columbia University, the University of Tokyo, and Ryukoku University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She served as professor at the University of Washington.
Conor Roddy is a philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin, where he studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Constance E. Kassor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College and Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, and later served on the faculty at Smith College.

Constance Powell Chin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her master's at San Jose State University under MA supervisor John W. Bernhardt, and also studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Regamey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw and the University of Paris, and later held professorships at the Universities of Warsaw, Lausanne (~1945-1977), and Fribourg (~1946-1977).

Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen, where he was supervised by Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1848-1853) and served as Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University (~1877-1901).
